_comment: The fixture corpus: one deal, three meetings, three months. Shaped so that
each downstream phase has something real to find -- see planted_cases.
Structural rows (account, deal, contacts, meetings) are inserted directly
because they need backdated timestamps the API will not accept. Documents
go through the real HTTP upload path, because that is what produces the
chunks and the offsets every label in labels/ points into.
Attendees are deliberately NOT seeded: deriving them from transcript
speaker labels is Phase 2.2, and seeding them would hide whether it works.

deal.name: SecureFlow Enterprise
deal._comment: Stage stays `discovery` though the transcripts clearly progress past it -- that is the stalled_stage risk, detectable with no model.

_contacts_comment: Tom Alvarez (procurement) and Dana Whitfield (CFO) speak in the transcripts but are deliberately absent here. Tom is the unresolved-attendee signal; Dana is the economic buyer whose arrival in meeting 3 should resolve no_economic_buyer.

contradiction.detail: Budget is stated as 'about a hundred and fifty thousand' with a board threshold in meeting 1, then 'two hundred and twenty thousand' approved by the CFO in meeting 3. The later fact must mark the earlier one superseded and keep both -- never overwrite.

unfulfilled_commitment.detail: Maya commits to sending the SOC 2 Type II 'by the seventh of August' in meeting 1. Meeting 2 opens with Priya saying it never arrived. A later commitment to send it 'this week' is made and, in meeting 3, implicitly satisfied -- the security review is complete.

spoken_number_literals.detail: Every amount and date is spoken, never written as a numeral: 'a hundred and fifty thousand', 'a hundred and sixty-two thousand', 'two hundred and twenty thousand', 'the seventh of August', 'Friday the twentieth'. A claim asserting '$150,000' or '2026-08-07' has no literal match in any span, so the rule must reject it unless a resolved record value holds that form. This is the fixture's sharpest test.

unresolved_attendee.exercises: Phase 2.3 entity resolution, the missing-stakeholder roll-up
unresolved_attendee.detail: Tom Alvarez speaks in all three meetings and is in no contact record. contact_id must stay NULL rather than being guessed onto Priya or Marcus.

economic_buyer_arrives.detail: No one who can approve spend attends meetings 1 or 2. Dana Whitfield (CFO) attends meeting 3 and approves. The risk should be open after meeting 2 and resolvable after meeting 3.

competitor_mention.detail: 'Vanta Logs' is named once, in meeting 1, and dismissed in the same breath. A detector that reads a single dismissed mention as active competitive pressure is producing a false positive -- the expensive kind here.

hard_dependency_objection.detail: Priya states in meeting 2 that security sign-off is a hard dependency, then states in meeting 3 that it is complete. An objection still rendered as open after meeting 3 means staleness is not working.

decision_criteria.detail: Normalisation on ingest with no customer-side adapters; twelve month retention; SCIM 2.0; a load test at nine million events before signature; fixed-fee professional services. Several are stated as conditions of signing rather than as wishes.
